fills.researcher_notes: Company-level Operator question for the Roadrunner/Coyanosa-to-San Elizario system, sourced here and not re-derived elsewhere in this brief (the other rows are Trans-Pecos/Comanche Trail/Rio Bravo/Valley Crossing, separate companies). ONEOK's own project page (oneok.com/rgt) names the operating entity as 'Roadrunner Gas Transmission, LLC', a 50/50 joint venture between an ONEOK subsidiary and Fermaca (a Mexico City infrastructure company); independently, worldpipelines.com's 2015 trade-press report on the project's launch corroborates the ONEOK/Fermaca 50/50 JV structure and the Coyanosa-to-San-Elizario route without tracing back to ONEOK's own release. Sheet Owner is currently 'ONEOK Inc [50.%]; Fermaca [50.%]', consistent with this JV structure -- Operator is the JV entity itself (Roadrunner Gas Transmission, LLC), distinct from but consistent with the two 50% owners. No merger churn applies to this entity name specifically (ONEOK's 2023 acquisition of Magellan does not touch the Roadrunner JV, which predates and is unrelated to Magellan's assets). Operator is written 'Roadrunner Gas Transmission, LLC' by the source; spelled the ownership team's way as 'Roadrunner Gas Transmission LLC'.
